clusters.title: The runtime ledger is a v1 feature that traces to no success criterion, journey or 00 0.5 row, and ADR 0006 records no 'not now' alternative under ADR 0005 rule 1.
clusters.scenario: ADR 0006's reason is that the data looks valuable; 13 13.9 names only later sessions and the maintainer as readers; 09 never runs ledger query, event list or event add; 12 12.2 orders the ledger before romeu-cli (run), so the first run waits on three stores, two mounts, ingest in four commands, I31 to I33 and their rows, for records nobody has needed yet.
clusters.change: Option 1 (keep in v1): add a 00 0.5 row for the ledger naming the need it serves (the 13 13.9 lessons loop and catalog-gap signal), and add to ADR 0006 a considered alternative 'not in v1; julieta state (08 8.2) and stderr are the record', with why it was rejected (events before the ledger exists are never recorded; adding the two mounts later costs one recreate per project, 13 13.1). Option 2 (defer): one Deferred row 'the runtime ledger (13; ADR 0006 stays the design)', until then julieta state (08 8.2) and stderr are the record, reopened by the first docs/lessons.md lesson naming a sandbox failure julieta state could not reconstruct, or by a second machine; 13 becomes a designed-not-built page like 06 6.6 and the mounts (03 3.3), ingest steps (04 4.2, 08 8.5), I31 to I33 and the ledger plan tasks leave v1.
clusters.cost: A maintainer decision; option 1 is a row and a paragraph, option 2 about a page of deletions across index, 03, 04, 05, 08, 12 and the plan.
clusters.resolution_text: Changes the scope (00 0.5) and the decision record ADR 0006 either way. Recommendation: option 1 only if the maintainer can name the consumer that needs events from the first run; otherwise option 2, since ADR 0005 prefers deferring and the cost of waiting (unrecorded early events, one recreate per project) is stated and small.
clusters.operator_reason: Changes the v1 scope (00 0.5) and ADR 0006.

clusters.title: A project created later under a retired project's name reads the retired project's entries, ids included, as its own, and no 05 5.4 row or deferred row carries it.
clusters.scenario: An operator retires 'api' from a past employer and later creates a personal 'api'; the new sandbox's own.jsonl and julieta event list show the earlier project's failures with their ids, which 13 13.2 says do not cross projects, while I33 promises a sandbox reads only its own project's entries whole.
clusters.change: Recommended smaller form: in 13 13.5 keep the sentence and add 'retire prints how many ledger entries the name holds, and that a project created later under this name reads them as its own'; in I33 add 'own means entries ingested under this project name, including a retired project's'; add a 05 5.4 row (accepted: in v1 the name is the identity; mitigation: the retire message) and a Deferred row 'a project identity other than its name (for example a generation-scoped view)', reopened by the first reuse of a retired name. Alternative (L16-5): sync of a name whose entries have no live or retired record refuses with a new error id unless confirmed on a TTY.
clusters.cost: One sentence in 13 13.5, one clause in I33, one risk row, one deferred row; or one rule, one error id and one test.
clusters.resolution_text: Recording the crossing as accepted adds a 05 5.4 row; the alternative adds a refusal. Recommendation: accept with the retire message and the deferred row, since the event fields are closed and the only agent-chosen value that crosses is `id`.

clusters.title: The no-delete rule binds the owner too, and the only remedy is rotation, which cannot apply to a project name the user chose and that every entry keeps.
clusters.scenario: A project named after a client ends and the client asks for removal; nothing lets the owner remove that project's entries, and a hand deletion leaves doctor failing on the view (04 4.2) with no recovery written.
clusters.change: In 13 13.5 add 'Owner removal: the rule binds romeu's code and agents; the operator may remove every entry of one project, or the whole ledger directory, by hand on the host, and the next ingest or doctor derives the views again without reporting a failure.' In the 05 5.4 secret row name the project name as the one user-chosen value the ledger keeps, with owner removal as its remedy. Record the distinction in ADR 0006 as a considered alternative.
clusters.cost: A paragraph, a row edit, a doctor behaviour (derive again rather than fail when entries are gone) and its test.
clusters.resolution_text: The absolute rule is the maintainer's (13 opening, ADR 0006) and the change edits a 05 5.4 row. Recommendation: accept owner removal as a stated limit of the rule; the 13 13.5 enforcement list already calls the host side a promise.
clusters.operator_reason: Narrows the maintainer's rule in ADR 0006 and edits an accepted risk in 05 5.4.

clusters.title: The spec records that six starting values and two residual risks were accepted with the design as a whole, not decided one by one.
clusters.scenario: A reviewer cannot tell a considered risk from one inherited with a block acceptance, and the block acceptance is how a feature the start may not need got in.
clusters.change: Either the maintainer decides the two 05 5.4 risks and the six 13 13.8 values by name, one quoted line each; or 05 5.4 marks the two rows 'inherited, undecided' and 13 13.8 keeps 'proposed defaults' and adds 'undecided' to its opening sentence.
clusters.cost: Eight one-line decisions, or two words per row.
clusters.resolution_text: Only the operator can decide an accepted risk. Recommendation: decide the two risks by name now (the merge decision needs them) and leave the six values marked proposed, since the index already has a deferred row that reopens them.
clusters.operator_reason: Changes the status of two accepted risks in 05 5.4.

clusters.title: The page never says the ledger stays on the machine, so 'the maintainer reads them to improve the product' and 'which error ids users hit' claim a cross-user reader that does not exist.
clusters.scenario: A secondary user's security team asks whether events are sent to the product's author and finds no sentence to quote; meanwhile the maintainer reads only their own ledger and concludes users hit no error ids, since each user's ledger stays local and romeu-side failures are not events.
clusters.change: In 13's opening replace 'later sessions and the maintainer read them to improve the product and the environment' with 'later sessions and the operator of this machine read them to improve the environment and, on the maintainer's machine, the product. The ledger never leaves the machine: no command sends, uploads or syncs it. It is always on, because a capture that depends on opting in is a capture an agent forgets.' In 13 13.9 change '(which error ids users hit)' to '(which error ids julieta hit on this machine)'. Add the never-leaves sentence to the README trust model (12 12.8).
clusters.cost: Three sentences.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply the wording; no opt-in export row and no romeu-side event now. The cross-machine gap is already the 'cross-machine sync of the ledger' and 'more event types and fields' deferred rows.

clusters.title: A session never sees its own events through julieta event list, because the view changes only at a host ingest, and no page says so; 'no failures' looks the same as 'not ingested yet'.
clusters.scenario: An agent records a note or sees julieta install fail, runs julieta event list, sees nothing new, and concludes everything ran clean or stops using the ledger.
clusters.change: In 13 13.9, under the table: 'A session sees its own events after the next romeu command that ingests (13 13.4); julieta event list prints first how many spool files are not yet in keys, so an empty list is not read as no failures.' In 04 4.3 event list, add the pending count to its output and a test row. Do not add ingest to stop or a SessionStart section.
clusters.cost: One count line in event list, its test row, about forty words.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply the latency sentence and the pending count; the smaller form drops the extra ingest in stop and the SessionStart output, which add a step to two more commands for a signal the count already gives.

clusters.title: The list of commands that ingest is hand-written in 13 13.4, 04 4.2 and 04 4.4, beside the other cross-cutting side effects, so a new command must remember to join it.
clusters.scenario: A later PR adds romeu prune; its author does not know ingest runs inside four commands; events written before a sandbox removal are lost with the spool, and the meta-test passes because it reads the same hand list.
clusters.change: Give each command definition an explicit side-effect field set (preflight, lock, ingest, drain, snapshot, appending) with no default, and add a 12 12.3 generator row rendering it as one table in 04 4.2 and 04 4.3; the idempotency meta-test and the T071 test read the definitions. In 13 13.4 replace the member list with 'Ingest runs inside each command whose definition says ingest (04 4.2), at the step that command names.' and keep the retire paragraph.
clusters.cost: One generator row, one field set per command definition, one generated table replacing five prose lists.
clusters.resolution_text: On page 13, delete the member list and link to the generated 04 table; the generator and the other four lists of L3-6 (git keys, memory allowlist, mise environment, reserved names) belong to the 04, 05, 07, 08 and 12 consolidations.

clusters.title: Every non-zero julieta exit emits command-failed, usage errors included, so an agent's typos become permanent entries that read like real failures.
clusters.scenario: An agent runs julieta memory show --josn and five other malformed calls; six command-failed entries enter the ledger for good, and the lessons loop counts a memory show failure trend that never existed.
clusters.change: In the 13 13.2 table of fields per type, make `ref` required for command-failed: 'required: the error id the command failed with'. In 13 13.9 add 'A usage error is told apart by its error id (exit class 2 of 04 4.1); the lessons loop filters on ref, not on exit_code.' No exclusion rule and no new member.
clusters.cost: One table cell, one sentence, one test row (a usage error yields a command-failed whose ref is the usage error id).
clusters.resolution_text: Smaller than excluding ids: the error id already names the usage error, so making ref required lets every consumer filter typos without a second rule.

clusters.title: The claim that every non-zero julieta exit emits command-failed is tested by one positive and three negatives, not over the command definitions.
clusters.scenario: A new command exits through os.Exit before the error mapping; its failures never reach the ledger and the lessons loop sees a quiet tool.
clusters.change: Add to 13 13.10 'Other rows': '**Emit coverage (U)**: for each command of the command definitions except hooks run, pane run and event, a forced failure yields exactly one command-failed event whose tool is that command's name and whose ref is the forced error id.'
clusters.cost: One table-driven test, one row.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as proposed, with the ref clause from R8-13-8.

clusters.title: Read compatibility is uneven: the manifest and the event specify an N and N-1 window tested only through an injected seam, while the other stored formats say nothing about another version.
clusters.scenario: romeu v1.3 bumps projects/<name>.json to version 2 and every version 1 record is refused, inviting a hurried migration that I16 forbids; meanwhile the event and manifest windows were chosen before any upgrade taught what breaks.
clusters.change: In 03's opening add one rule for every format: 'A reader accepts its own version. Where a section names a window (the manifest, 03 3.6; the event, 13 13.7) it also accepts N-1. Every other format accepts exactly its own version in v1; the first release that bumps one adds its window and its test in the same change, and a new version is additive. Stored ledger entries are never migrated; an owner that rewrites its file whole writes its current version on its next write.' In 13 13.7, after 'In v1 the window holds one version', add 'so the N-1 rows of 13.10 prove the seam, and the first release that adds a version proves the window.'
clusters.cost: One paragraph in 03 and one sentence in 13 13.7; no new ADR, no new error id.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply as one rule plus a stated limit; it keeps ADR 0006's N and N-1 window unchanged and does not add the product-wide ADR L3-3 proposed. Primary home is the 03 consolidation.

clusters.title: One idea, the format version, has three spellings: apiVersion: romeu/v1, an integer version, and schema: runtime-event/v1.
clusters.scenario: A contributor adds a new schema and picks a fourth form; a generic reader needs to know a file's family before it can find its version.
clusters.change: In 03's opening choose one form for every schema of 02 2.1 (recommended: the `schema: <name>/v<n>` string the ledger's three formats already use, which names the format as well as the version), apply it to every example, and have tools/ci schema fail a schema without the field in that form. Page 13 keeps its text if the ledger's form is chosen.
clusters.cost: A decision, a sentence, regenerated schemas and examples before T021.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply in 03 with the ledger's form; page 13 keeps its text. Primary home is the 03 consolidation.

Have tools/new command print that sentence. The id width (two or three digits) is decided in 04. Page 13 keeps 13 13.7 as the home and needs no change.

clusters.title: ledger-entry/v1 and the view files have no JSON Schema although 03 says every format has one.

In 03's opening name them as the exemptions. The pin-file and mutation-surface parts of L3-34 go to the 02, 05 and 10 consolidations.

clusters.title: Ledger ids are lowercase ULIDs for an APFS reason while memory, handoff, candidate, generation and salvage ids are uppercase, and the stores use three timestamp naming pairs.

clusters.change: In 03 3.12 add one rule: every ULID romeu or julieta writes into a file name is lowercase Crockford, for the reason 13 13.2 gives; and one sentence per store saying why its timestamp names differ (writer-set versus romeu-stamped). Page 13 keeps its text.
clusters.cost: One rule and a few renamed fields before code exists.
clusters.resolution_text: Apply the lowercase rule in 03 3.12; for timestamps, state the reason per store rather than rename. Primary home is the 03 consolidation.
